author: EmuCore - Hub
title: CAN Duckstation's Downsampling IMPROVE PS1 Graphics? - Affro's Curiosities
summary: Affro's Curiosities tests DuckStation downsampling against PS1 games that combine sharp 3D geometry with low-resolution two-dimensional artwork.
searchKeywords: CAN Duckstation's Downsampling IMPROVE PS1 Graphics? - Affro's Curiosities

blocks.text: The video starts from a familiar PS1 enhancement problem: a high internal resolution can sharpen polygons while leaving backgrounds, menus or sprites comparatively soft. It tests whether rendering high and then downsampling changes that mismatch. The result is a visual comparison, not a universal prescription. A useful viewer should compare the same scene's edges, texture detail and interface readability rather than interpreting a cleaner three-dimensional model as an improvement to every layer.

Downsampling cannot recreate detail that was never present in a source texture; it changes how samples are combined for final output. Display scaling and YouTube compression can also hide or exaggerate the difference. Try the option on a personal game dump at the display's native size and keep the game's default rendering as a reference. If a scene depends on original dithering or a special blend effect, assess those elements separately before deciding the overall image is better.
